cards.explanation: The answer is the way to walk and what to do. The people ask Jeremiah to pray that the LORD will tell them "…the way we should walk and the thing we should do." They want directions, and they say they'll follow them. I think a lot of us would sign up for that before breakfast, friends.

The answer is True. Jeremiah tells them, "I will not withhold a word from you." He also says he'll pray as they ask and tell them everything the LORD answers. Nothing gets trimmed off the edges, friends.

The answer is that it will make it go well with them. They say they'll obey so that "…it may go well with us when we obey the voice of the LORD our God!" They say it before they even hear the answer, pleasant or unpleasant. That's a big promise to make with the oven door still shut, bakers.

The answer is stay. The LORD says, "If you will indeed stay in this land, then I will build you up and not tear you down…" The offer is on the table, and it starts with staying put. Simple, but I think staying put is harder than it sounds when you're scared, friends.
The answer is afraid. The LORD says, "Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear…" He says it twice in a row. When God repeats Himself, I lean in, bakers.

The answer is that He is with them to save them. The LORD says, "…for I am with you to save you and deliver you from him." The reason not to be afraid is not a changed situation, it's who is with them. That's a better reason than any I ever had in the dark, friends.

The answer is being restored to their own land. The LORD says, "And I will show you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and restore you to your own land." Compassion and a way back home, together. That's a good box of news, bakers.
The answer is Egypt. The second if has them saying, "No, but we will go to the land of Egypt and live there…" Egypt is the place they picture for a fresh start, friends.

The answer is war and hunger. They picture Egypt as a place "…where we will not see war or hear the sound of the ram’s horn or hunger for bread…" War and hunger are the two things they say they won't face there. That's the picture they paint in the LORD's second if, bakers.

The answer is that they will follow them into Egypt. The LORD says "…the sword you fear will overtake you there, and the famine you dread will follow on your heels into Egypt…" The very things they fear and dread come along with them, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I will bring upon them." That's about all who resolve to go to Egypt to live there. It's a heavy line, and I think it's meant to be taken seriously, bakers.

The answer is the land they're in now. The LORD says, "…you will never see this place again." That's the land they're standing in as Jeremiah speaks. It's a sober line, so I'll leave it right there, friends.

The answer is deceived. Jeremiah says, "For you have deceived yourselves by sending me to the LORD your God…" They said they'd do whatever the LORD said, and Jeremiah says they've fooled themselves. I think that's the hardest kind of fooling, bakers.

The answer is False. Jeremiah says, "…you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God in all He has sent me to tell you." He's not praising them, he's pointing out they haven't done it. It's a hard thing to hear, friends.
